chunks: Look, when I die from this stroke of his, then strike him one stroke for his stroke, and do not dismember the man, for I have heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'Beware of mutilation, even if it is for a rabid dog.'

key_terms.ضَرْبَةٌ بِضْرَبَةٍ: one stroke for one stroke (proportional retribution)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on mutilation during execution according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) instructs Hasan and Husayn to execute Ibn Muljam with a single, proportional strike corresponding to the fatal blow, explicitly avoiding *al-muthlah* (mutilation) by not dismembering the body. He grounds this ruling in the Prophet’s hadith that forbids mutilation even for a rabid dog, establishing a principle of justice that distinguishes between retribution and excessive disfigurement. This instruction highlights the Shia emphasis on adhering to prophetic precedent in legal execution, ensuring that punishment remains dignified and precise rather than vengeful.
